title: Pseudodipteral
wikitext:
[[File:Selinunte-TempleG-Plan-bjs.svg|thumb|The plan of temple "G" in Selinunte]]
'''Pseudodipteral''' or '''Pseudodipteros''' ({{langx|el|ψευδοδίπτερος}}, meaning “falsely dipteral”)<ref>[https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.04.0059:entry=pseudodipteros Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, A Latin Dictionary, pseudodipteros]</ref><ref>[https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.04.0062:entry=pseudodipteros-harpers Harry Thurston Peck, Harpers Dictionary of Classical Antiquities (1898), pseudodipteros]</ref> describes an [[ancient Greek temple]] with a single [[peristyle]] surrounding the [[cella]] at the distance of two intercolumns and one column.<ref name="Vitruvius2009">{{cite book|author=Vitruvius|title=On Architecture|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lBLNbOp46CYC&pg=PT350|date=24 September 2009|publisher=Penguin Books Limited|isbn=978-0-14-193195-1|pages=350–}}</ref> Unlike [[peripteral]] temples, there is a greater space between the columns of the peristyle and the cella; [[Glossary of architecture#D|dipteral]] temples have two peristyles.

Temple "G" in [[Selinunte]], an ancient Greek archaeological site in Italy, is a good example of the pseudodipteral plan.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.kaoscollective.com/portfolio/temple-g/ | title=Kaos Collective > Temple G }}</ref>

extract:
Pseudodipteral or Pseudodipteros (Greek: ψευδοδίπτερος, meaning “falsely dipteral”) describes an ancient Greek temple with a single peristyle surrounding the cella at the distance of two intercolumns and one column. Unlike peripteral temples, there is a greater space between the columns of the peristyle and the cella; dipteral temples have two peristyles.
Temple "G" in Selinunte, an ancient Greek archaeological site in Italy, is a good example of the pseudodipteral plan.
